title: Cookies: Website Memory
drDigitalIntro:
A cookie is a small note a website leaves on your computer so it can remember you.
• Some cookies help you. A cookie is why a shop still has your basket after you close the page, and why you do not have to log in every single time.
• Some cookies watch you. Advertisers put the same cookie on many sites, then follow you from one to the next and build up a picture of what you read and what you buy.
• That is why sites ask. When a cookie banner appears, Decline is a safe answer. The page still works, and you have said no to being followed.

steps.say: Go to weather.com — type it and press Enter. Many sites greet you with a cookie notice.
A cookie banner appeared at the bottom. Click Decline to say no to tracking cookies. The site still works fine without them.

drDigitalSuccess: You declined the tracking cookies. The site works exactly as well without them, and the advertisers lost the trail. Decline is the safe answer unless you have a reason to say otherwise.
drDigitalHint: Look at the dark bar across the bottom of the page and click the Decline button.
